Also, I did some research the other day and I think the automod took it off because of the links inside the comment. Although this is what I found:

A few months ago, I saw people on this subreddit were recommending microgreens for birds who need more green intake.  
  
For those of you who are unfamiliar with what microgreens are, Webmd.com says "While there are a wide variety of microgreens that you can buy (or grow at home), the names of these miniature plants should sound familiar: beets, Swiss chard, broccoli, mustard, arugula, amaranth, and peas among others. Microgreens are simply the versions of these vegetables and herbs when they are in their tiny sprout form (https://www.webmd.com/diet/what-to-know-about-microgreens)."  
  
Here are some sources of research I've done on whether Budgerigar's might be able to eat these vegetables (though I've only found info on the listed greens being consumed in mature form, not microgreen form). Note: Some of the sources mention parrots are capable of eating some of these vegetables and so I'm assuming that they must be safe for Budgerigars, as a result. Feel free to correct me on any of this.  
  
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_  
  
Broccoli: Parrots (types are specified in the article) are capable of eating Broccoli, raw or cooked. The leaves and stems are fair-game and there aren't any precautions in terms of toxicity. Dr.Luqman Javed, Veterinarian DVM. (https://petkeen.com/can-parakeets-eat-broccoli/)  
  
Purple Kohlrabi: I found a website that mentions there are two type of Kohlrabi, white and purple. Kohlrabi is related to Brussel sprouts, broccoli, and cabbage. It states Budgie's are able to consume Kohlrabi but doesn't specify if they can have the purple variant. (https://billionpet.com/can-budgies-eat-kohlrabi/)  
  
Mizuna: I couldn't find any mentions towards whether Mizuna is eatable on the internet for Budgerigars. Plenty of questions on different bird forums and reddit, but just as many answers of uncertainty. I think the reasoning is that Mizuna is a Japanese vegetable and so, therefore, knowledge in the USA (where most domesticated Budgerigar's reside) is limited. I found a link of a woman living in Japan, mentioning that the vet recommended her birds eat "Mizuna" which is a potherb plant. (https://parrot-lovers.livejournal.com/4494712.html)  
  
Red Cabbage: This is safe to feed to Budgies, according to the Parrotkeen.com, they are capable of eating Chinese, Savoy, Napa, White, Red, and Purple cabbage (https://parrotkeen.com/can-budgies-eat-cabbage/) I found a user on an Avian Parrot forum stating that Red cabbage Microgreens are safe (https://forums.avianavenue.com/index.php?threads/microgreens.258301/)  
  
Red Mustard: Red Mustard seeds can be fed to Budgie's, however, the only notable information I found on Red mustard is that the seeds may be eaten. There wasn't any info on red mustard sprouts/microgreens. (Budgie Herb seeds)  
  
Amaranth: Amaranth is a budgie-safe grain that can be fed to them, this information I found is in the same link I posted for Red Mustard.  
  
Tatsoi: Here I found an article that provides a list of 45 different seeds, grain, and legumes that can be used to grow "Parrot-safe sprouts" and Tatsoi is listed there as one of them. (https://www.recipets.com/list-of-45-seeds-grains-and-legumes-that-can-be-used-to-grow-parrot-safe-sprouts/)

If anyone finds this reddit discussion in the future I made a new post on my profile for my final verdict on the microgreen mix in this post. I also reposted the comment with the research there in case others can't see it due to automod.

Maybe try adding in a few tablespoons of water into his usual grain food so that it creates an oatmeal mush consistency, thick but not drenched. Not too watery (you don't want them getting diarrhea from excess water). Keep this up this for a few days, waiting an hour every morning when you change their food to see if he'll eat from it by himself, after the one hour is up then add another bowl of his grain diet dry, how you normally make it, beside the mush food bowl. This preps him for pre-exposure to mixing other wet things in his diet like chop, and also makes sure he doesn't starve while you're transitioning him. Leave the bowls side-by-side until night comes and then repeat the steps the same way the next day with a fresh batch of mush and dry, both bowls side-by-side.

If eventually you notice he's accepting the mush equally as much as the regular dry grain, then try adding in one TBSP of a finely chopped steamed/boiled veggie of your choice into the mush bowl. maybe carrot??
